note: Zabt introduced under Akbar — Todar Mal's 10-year survey, 1570-1580 (gess104 p. 43).
Birbal is not named anywhere in gess104 or lehs205 (Theme 9). The chapter teaches Akbar's murid (disciple) circle and eclectic worship, but the member's name is not in the NCERT books used.
Persian made the language of the court (by Akbar) and of administration at all levels (lehs205, Theme 9).
Todar Mal, Akbar's revenue minister, and the zabt system (gess104 p. 43; lehs205 on Todar Mal as finance minister).
Duh-Aspah Sih-Aspah is a mansabdari detail from Themes II Theme 8, which could not be fetched; not in gess104 or lehs205. Source gap, not a scope choice.
Jadunath Sarkar is modern historiography; no NCERT textbook chapter used names him. Not teachable from the allowed sources.
Babur wrote his memoirs in Turkish; Akbar Nama/Humayun Nama were written by others (lehs205). Section s1 also introduces the memoirs.
Sulh-i kul promoted by Akbar (gess104 p. 44; lehs205 Theme 9, sulh-i kul as cornerstone of enlightened rule).
The Sisodiya Rajputs of Mewar refused Mughal authority the longest (gess104 p. 41); also in the chapter's exam_note box and the book's own match exercise (Sisodiya Rajput — Mewar).
The Satnami rebellion is covered in Themes II Theme 8 (not fetched) — absent from gess104 and lehs205. Source gap.
The Mahabharata was translated as the Razmnama (Book of Wars) (lehs205, Theme 9).
Ain-i Akbari is the third book of Abul Fazl's Akbar Nama (lehs205; gess104 p. 43).

Jaswant Singh received the title Mirza Raja from Aurangzeb (lehs205) — so he belongs to Aurangzeb's reign, not Akbar's; the chapter teaches Akbar's contemporaries (Bharmal, Todar Mal, Abul Fazl) for elimination.
Same gap as Q177 (2016): Birbal is not named in the two NCERT books used.
Official key: Aurangzeb. Neither gess104 nor lehs205 discusses a prohibition of sati, so the chapter neither teaches nor contradicts the key. Flagged as a source gap in REPORT.md.
Akbar's quest led to interfaith debates in the ibadat khana at Fatehpur Sikri (lehs205, Theme 9).
Mansab = position or rank; zat/sawar explained (lehs205; gess104 match exercise 'Mansab: Rank').
The ten-year (dahsala) assessment system under Akbar is taught in full (Todar Mal's 1570-1580 survey); the term 'Ain-i-Dahsala' itself is glossed in the section's definition box.
Buland Darwaza at Akbar's Fatehpur Sikri, built to recall the Gujarat victory (lehs205, Theme 9).

The term 'Tulghumah' does not appear in the books used. The chapter teaches Babur's effective use of cannons/artillery at Panipat (gess104 p. 40), which points to Babur but does not teach the named tactic.
Abul Fazl fell victim to a conspiracy hatched by Prince Salim; murdered by Bir Singh Bundela (lehs205, Theme 9).
Dara Shikoh's Upanishad translation (Sirr-i Akbar) is not mentioned in gess104 or lehs205 (Dara appears only in a wedding caption). Source gap.
Humayun Nama written by Gulbadan Begum, Babur's daughter (lehs205, Theme 9).
The Sikh Gurus belong to the Bhakti-Sufi chapter (HIS-12) and later Mughal-Sikh relations; not in the two books used for this chapter.
Alamgir was a title of Aurangzeb (lehs205, Theme 9, on chronicle titles including Alamgir Nama).
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526 (gess104 p. 40).

The founder is taught: Akbar's self-conceived eclectic divine worship and his circle of disciples (murid) are covered in s6; the label 'Din-i Ilahi' appears in the question itself. The s6 exam_note box states this openly.

The chapter teaches the fact and year of the translation (Babur Nama, 1589 — lehs205 timeline), but neither book names Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khanan as translator. Partially covered; marked not-taught because the asked fact (the translator) is not in the sources.
Mir Jumla presenting the Kohinoor to Shah Jahan is not in gess104 or lehs205. Source gap.

Sher Shah's road (Sadak-e-Azam, East Bengal to Peshawar) is not described in the two NCERT books used; s2 says this openly in its exam_note box. This is the chapter's biggest known PYQ gap — the WBBSE Class VII book (unfetchable here) normally covers Sher Shah's administration.
Akbar abolished the tax on pilgrimage in 1563 (lehs205, Theme 9).
Padmavat's completion under Sher Shah is not in the books used (same Sher Shah source gap as Q65).
Assam's non-annexation is not stated in gess104 or lehs205 (the texts say the empire covered nearly the whole subcontinent without naming Assam as the exception). Not taught rather than guessed.
Brahmajit Gaur is an obscure detail absent from all NCERT/WBBSE school texts checked; same Sher Shah source gap.
Akbar decided to build the new capital Fatehpur Sikri in the 1570s (lehs205, Theme 9).

Mansur is not named in the books used; the painters the chapter can source are Mir Sayyid Ali, Abdus Samad, Abu'l Hasan, Payag and Bishandas. A student cannot identify the unmentioned painter from the chapter text alone.
Taccavi (agricultural loans) is Themes II Theme 8 material — that PDF could not be fetched. Source gap.
Guru Tegh Bahadur's execution is not mentioned in gess104 or lehs205. Source gap (the fact is standard, but no fetched source states it).

Taught by context: s8 covers Thomas Roe's embassy to Jahangir's court and English contact beginning in his reign (lehs205), with Jahanara's Surat revenues in s7. The 1613 Surat farman itself is not quoted in the NCERT texts — noted honestly in REPORT.md.
Khutba is a Sultanate-era concept belonging to HIS-10; not defined in the books used here.
Tulsidas and the Ramcharitmanas belong to the Bhakti chapter (HIS-12). Out of this chapter's scope.
The mismatched pair (Ajmer — Quwwat-ul-Islam) is Sultanate architecture, belonging to HIS-10. Out of scope here.
Chand Bibi of Ahmednagar belongs to the Deccan Sultanates in HIS-10. Out of scope here.
